ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), as amended by the AML package of 22 December 2023 (core UBO register obligations effective 1 July 2025); Swiss Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220) Art. 697j et seq. (private register of beneficial owners of non-listed stock companies and GmbH, accessible exclusively to competent authorities, not public); Swiss Criminal Code (SCC, SR 311.0) Art. 305bis and 305ter; Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO, SR 955.01); FINMA Circular 2023/02 on Money Laundering; Federal Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions ordinances implementing UN and Swiss autonomous sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Commercial Registry or Registrar of Companies in the country of origin of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention member state) OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of identity document (passport) of each shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized or bank-issued source-of-funds and bank reference letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank / financial institution maintaining the relevant accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; additionally attested by Swiss licensed fiduciary where the bank's signature is not apostillable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of legalization itself (Apostille certificate / consular endorsement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Secretary of State, or designated issuing authority in the document's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (ii) SECO Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs sanctions and embargo lists, (iii) OFAC SDN List (relevant for USD and Stripe settlement rails), (iv) EU and UK consolidated lists as banking-counterparty risk matter, and (v) FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. Enhanced due diligence is required under AMLA Art. 5 for foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including documented verification of the origin of funds and of the personal wealth of the PEP. Adverse-media screening and beneficial-ownership chain verification are mandatory per FINMA Circular 2023/02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex, www.zefix.ch); actual name clearance and registration are filed through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office; official publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / SOGC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the principle of truthfulness of company names (Art. 950 CO), the name must truthfully describe the activity and must not mislead. The name may be in German, French, Italian, Romansh or any other language, provided it is written using the Latin alphabet and contains the mandatory legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' denoting Aktiengesellschaft. Foreign-words must be transliterated into recognizable Latin script and must not violate the principle of due disclosure of legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of the written rejection issued by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (Handelsregister-Aufsichtsbehörde), annexing the original clearance application, the rejection decision and full legal grounds; further appeal lies to the cantonal Administrative Court and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht), each within 30 days of service. The applicant may without prejudice concurrently re-file the name clearance application using modified wording that addresses the stated grounds for rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a licensed Swiss domiciliation provider maintaining a substantive physical registered office at the designated Swiss address and providing a responsible local service address. An AG must have its registered office in Switzerland (Art. 50 CO), with the administration located at a genuine place of administration; a pure virtual office with no physical presence and no responsible local person will be rejected by the commercial register and may trigger dissolution proceedings. For a Logistics_Tech_SaaS business assessed as Low_Risk_Standard, a licensed domiciliation office in the canton of the registered office is accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated below 5% over the first five years for a low-risk Logistics_Tech_SaaS profile), but materially higher where the registered office is a mass-domiciliation address, where nominee-like structures are detected, or where PEP, sanctions or tax red flags arise. Unannounced on-site visits may be conducted by the commercial register supervisory authority, cantonal tax authorities, and the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) without prior warning.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public notarization of the deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial statutory tariff; flat CHF 1,500–2,500 plus approximately 0.1% of nominal share capital (CHF 100,000); Zurich/Zug benchmark CHF 2,400–3,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee (Handelsregister-Eintragung) for Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal and cantonal registry fee schedule for AG incorporation; CHF 600–1,200; benchmark CHF 800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and licensed domiciliation service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CHF 2,500–4,000 per annum per AG

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Articles of Association (Statuten), incorporation resolutions, and ancillary corporate contracts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP / sanctions / adverse-media screening of shareholders, directors, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss law firm or third-party AML screening vendor

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, OR/CO), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / stock corporation); Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code, Part Five, Arts. 716a-731b (corporate governance and board duties); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung / Ordonnance sur le registre du commerce, ORC) Arts. 23-35.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Kantonales Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce), acting under the supervisory authority of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt / Office fédéral du registre du commerce, EHRA/OFAC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Incorporation and Application for Registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister / Demande d'inscription au registre du commerce), together with the notarized Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an AG is CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 (or 20% of the nominal capital if higher) must be fully paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up amount must be deposited into a blocked Swiss bank escrow account (Sperrkonto / compte de consignation) in the company's name and released only upon proof of registration. The remaining capital must be subscribed and payable on demand.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors resolves: (1) that the company's incorporation be executed by accepting the notarized Articles of Association and the required share subscriptions; (2) that the share capital of CHF 100,000 is subscribed as stated and the statutory minimum paid-up amount shall be deposited in the company's blocked bank account; (3) that the company adopts the registered office at the address indicated in the Articles and appoints the registered address for service; (4) that [Name] is appointed Managing Director (Delegate) with individual signing authority and [Name] is appointed Assistant with collective signing authority; (5) that all incorporation filings and banking formalities are authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notar / Notaire) designated by the cantonal commercial registry; in most cantons, a licensed notary in the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company charter in the official Swiss language of the canton (usually German, French, or Italian). Submit the draft Articles to the notary together with identity documents and the founders' capital subscription statements. The notary shall certify the incorporation deed and verify that the statutory minimum capital provisions and capital band provisions are met. After notarization, the notary issues certified copies for commercial register filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts) signed by founders
Notarized fractional shares/units declaration (if applicable)
Founder identification (passport or national ID) certified copies
Founder declaration of no insolvency and no disqualification
Schedule of capital subscriptions and proposed board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the draft (e.g., missing capital band, improper name, or non-compliant clauses), the founders shall amend the Articles and re-submit the corrected deed. Any capital escrow deficiency must be remedied by increasing the paid-up deposit before notarization is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-up Share Capital in Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed securities dealer operating in Switzerland (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, Raiffeisen, or recognized Swiss fintech bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked corporate account in the company's intended name at a Swiss bank. Transfer the mandatory paid-up amount (min. CHF 50,000, or 20% of nominal capital) by wire from unrestricted funds. Instruct the bank to issue an escrow confirmation letter (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung / attestation de blocage) addressed to the commercial register. The account cannot be released without the commercial register's consent or the company's proof of registration.
required_dossiers: Draft or certified Articles of Association
Genehmigung (founders' resolution) for opening the escrow account
Identification of beneficial owners and signatories
Bank account opening application and AML declarations
Confirmation of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the escrow confirmation is rejected due to insufficient funding or bank compliance concerns, the founders must immediately wire the shortfall, provide clearer source-of-funds evidence, or engage a different authorized bank. If bank compliance timeout occurs, re-initiate the process with a different licensed financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Commercial Register Application and Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Kantonales Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) where the registered office of the AG is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official registration application with the cantonal commercial register via its electronic portal (e.g., soi-app or cantonal e-forms) or in physicalized paper form if the canton requires. Include the notarized deed, the escrow bank confirmation, the signed list of directors with signatures, and the declaration that the capital has been lawfully subscribed and paid. Pay the filing fee and await the register's verification of legal compliance. Upon approval, the commercial register shall issue a certificate of incorporation (Handelsregisterauszug / extrait du registre du commerce).
required_dossiers: Completed application form for commercial register entry (Anmeldung / Demande d'inscription)
Public deed of incorporation (notarized statutes and capital subscription report)
Bank escrow confirmation letter proving paid-up capital
Board of directors' declarations of acceptance of office and signature specimen
Statutory declaration of legality (Willenserklärung / Déclaration relative à la loi)
Notice of official registered office and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial register issues a temporary refusal or a request for additional evidence (e.g., name conflict, deficient bank confirmation, or unclear powers of attorney), the applicant may file a cure letter within the statutory deadline, amend the offending document, and re-submit. If the register rejects due to a reserved company name, file a name change petition or request a written refusal which can be appealed to the cantonal supervisory commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in Swiss Official Gazette and Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt / Feuille officielle suisse du commerce, SHAB/FOSC); subsequent cantonal tax authorities and Federal Statistical Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Automatic publication of the commercial register entry in SHAB/FOSC. After receiving the official certificate, the company must complete VAT registration with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) if turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year (or voluntarily), and register for AHV/social security for employees. Obtain a business identification number (UID) and, if physical office premises, business premises clearance from the cantonal authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (Handelsregisterauszug / Extrait du registre du commerce)
Notification of official publication excerpt from SHAB
Articles of association as registered
Corporate UID number assignment confirmation
VAT registration form (formular 101) for relevant taxable services
Employment documents (if personnel hired), including AHV registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is queried due to incorrect SIC/NACE classification, refile with accurate description of fleet telematics SaaS. If UID notification is delayed, contact the Swiss Federal Statistical Office to request duplicate certification. Any post-registration rectification must be filed via the cantonal commercial register office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing board for ISIC 6201 computer programming and telematics SaaS; the entity conducts no physical manufacturing or warehousing operation requiring an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required (non-industrial software and data services; no manufacturing permit or cantonal industrial operating license is triggered).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt / Office fédéral de l'environnement, BAFU/OFEV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category Not Listed; the activity is a pure software/telematics service with no physical installations, heavy emissions, or environmental medium impact.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated discharge or emission thresholds apply to the software facility. If an office is occupied, general municipal waste handling and water discharge standards apply, and any incidental IT hardware waste must be disposed of in accordance with the Swiss Ordinance on the Return, Take-back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORDEE).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and building regulations: the registered office must comply with cantonal building standards, including fire safety evacuation plans and electrical installations certificates. No industrial workplace or civil defense clearance is required because the activity is office-based administrative. The employer must comply with Swiss Labour Law and the Safety at Work Ordinance (Verordnung über die Sicherheit von Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern, VSA/ArGV 3), including workplace ergonomics and accident prevention; for any staff, mandatory accident insurance (SUVA) and workplace hazard assessments are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), Bern — for federal direct tax and Swiss VAT; Cantonal and municipal tax authorities of the registered office for cantonal/communal corporate income tax; Register of Commerce authorities in the relevant Canton for commercial registration. Official portals: www.estv.admin.ch and www.zefix.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Swiss Aktiengesellschaft: (1) establish the company by notarial deed and register it in the Commercial Register of the Canton (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce); minimum paid-in capital is CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be actually paid-up at registration; (2) upon commercial entry, the business is automatically assigned a Swiss Business Identifier (UID / Unternehmensidentifikationsnummer) in the format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx; (3) if the actual or expected worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per annum, or if voluntary or reverse-charge registration is appropriate, submit the VAT registration application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) through its eService platform; the UID is then used as the VAT identification number (MWST-Nr.); (4) Swiss corporate income tax registration is effected automatically by the cantonal tax authority once the legal entity is entered in the Commercial Register; a separate tax ID for direct tax purposes is issued by the canton of domicile and used on tax returns and payment orders. No shareholder residency restriction applies to a Swiss AG; but foreign founders must appoint at least one resident director and furnish bank verification, certified articles, passport copies and sworn statements as requested by the commercial registrar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A Swiss AG is statutorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax at federal, cantonal and municipal levels, plus net wealth tax; no pass-through taxation is available. Within that fixed classification, the AG may invoke the following elections and reliefs: (a) participation relief/deduction (Beteiligungsabzug) for dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10% of the investee's share capital to 10% per analog; typically requiring quality of interest and at least 12 months holding, effectively exempting such income; (b) notional interest deduction (NID) where the canton of residence has implemented it for equity financing over the business need; (c) cantonal patent/IP box regimes and R&D bonus bonuses under the Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF); (d) VAT flat-rate input tax credit (Saldosteuersätze) election for smaller businesses; (e) VAT method election between the effective net tax method and the rates/quota-based method; (f) tax-neutral reorganisation rules under Art. 61 et seq. of the Federal Direct Tax Act for mergers, demergers, and share-for-share reorganisations; (g) qualified holding company tax status at cantonal level in certain cantons (subject to transitional and TRAF limitations). Hybrid mismatch treatment is not elective; Swiss anti-avoidance and transfer pricing rules apply by law and reporting is through the OECD country-by-country framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) / Mehrwertsteuer (MWST) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 as amended, administered by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); no GST or sales-and-use tax exists at federal level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (general threshold, excluding exempt supplies); CHF 150,000 for tax-exempt charitable non-profit entities; foreign-domiciled taxable persons must register if their taxable supplies in Switzerland exceed the threshold, unless the recipient is liable for Swiss VAT by reverse charge and the supplier is exempt from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate a real-time fiscal clearing, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping system. Electronic invoices are valid for VAT purposes and must contain the full statutory invoice data under Art. 26 MWSTG (supplier name and UID, recipient, date, description, consideration, and applicable tax rate). In B2G practice, the Swiss federal administration has been encouraging e-procurement invoices via eBill and XML/QR-bill standards, but there is no national e-invoicing clearance obligation imposed by the tax authority. VAT returns are filed electronically through the FTA eService portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Switzerland to a destination outside the Swiss customs territory are eligible for the 0% VAT rate provided the supplier proves the goods were physically exported and delivered abroad. Services directly linked to exported goods (freight, handling, inspection, packing, protective activities) supplied to a person abroad may also be zero-rated. For software-as-a-service, fleet telematics, and optimisation services supplied by a Swiss AG to a foreign business customer, Swiss VAT is generally not due because the place of supply of B2B services is the customer's country of establishment; where Swiss VAT is still technically imposed due to the Swiss place-of-supply rule, zero-rating may be claimed if the recipient is established outside Switzerland and the service is provided to that foreign recipient. The AG must maintain and produce on request all documents proving the export or foreign-delivery nature of the transaction, including contracts, invoices, customs receipts, and records of actual use or consumption abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e-dec / GemData export declaration) accepted by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration
Commercial invoice with complete supplier and consignee identification
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Customs export accompanying document (Ausfuhrbegleitpapier / document d'accompagnement exportation)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence demonstrating foreign-currency payment repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may retroactively deny export zero-rating and claw back the VAT if the taxpayer does not produce complete documentary evidence within the assessment period. Fraudulent or simulated export transactions to obtain VAT advantages constitute tax evasion under Art. 76 of the VAT Act and can lead to penalties of up to four times the tax evaded, plus interest, in addition to the revocation of the zero-rating and input VAT deductions. Records, including export documents, must be retained for at least 10 years under the Swiss VAT accounting rules. The FTA may initiate criminal proceedings under the Swiss Administrative Penal Code, and directors appointed to the AG may be personally liable for penalties if the evasion is attributable to organisational fault.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF); foreign exchange monitoring is decentralized with mandatory reporting to SNB for positions exceeding CHF 20 million for non-bank financial counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full capital and current account convertibility under the libre circulation of payments principle embedded in the Federal Constitution and the Federal Foreign Exchange and Payment Transactions Act. There are no surrender requirements, prior authorization hurdles, or profit remittance restrictions. Swiss francs (CHF) are freely convertible; legal tender is not capital-controlled, and dividends, royalties, and service fees may be repatriated without withholding tax on profits except for the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax on dividends, which is reduced under tax treaties. No stamp duties or exchange control approvals are required for routine operational flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists. Swiss law permits exporters and SaaS service providers to retain proceeds in original currency, hold offshore accounts, or convert freely through regulated banks. Only statistical reporting obligations apply under the SNB Banking Statistics Ordinance for international trans-shipment and billing positions above a materiality threshold, with no administrative conversion mandate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for non-licensed offshore Electronic Money Institutions. Switzerland is not part of the EEA/EMI Directive framework; foreign EMI licenses under UK FCA or EU PSD2 do not grant passporting rights into Switzerland. A foreign fintech/EMI may only provide payment services to Swiss clients through a Swiss-regulated bank as a white-label corridor or after obtaining a FINMA fintech licence (art. 1b Swiss Banking Act) and establishing a Swiss presence. Strict FINMA outsourcing and data protection requirements also apply, and non-bank issuers cannot provide full credit-scope treasury services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not always mandatory but is strongly preferred by tier-1 commercial banks. Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and FINMA Circular 2023/1, identification may be completed through a certified Swiss notary, a Swiss-regulated financial intermediary, or an equivalent foreign regulated entity that performs the face-to-face identification. Remote video identification is accepted if the bank's internal procedure meets electronic identification standards (FINMA-AEOI circular and Swiss Code of Obligations record-keeping requirements). In practice, at least one beneficial owner or director may be asked for an interview at a Swiss branch or at the branch of the bank's correspondent before opening billing or capital escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership traced to a non-resident shareholder through a multi-tier trust or holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed UBO declaration per FINMA/OBA form, notarized statutory identification of all natural persons in the chain, audited corporate ownership register from the commercial registry, bank reference letters from existing relationship institutions, and certified source-of-funds documentation including asset backstopping records and dividend/equity contribution evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions to logistics counterparties in counterparty-risk jurisdictions without a clear business rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export and import customs declarations, commercial invoices and bills of lading, freight forwarding contracts, route telematics reports generated from the fleet-dispatch SaaS, sworn logistics chain-of-custody documentation, and a bank-reviewed sanctions and adverse-media screening dossier for every jurisdictional counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented high-frequency distributed subscriptions and transaction receipts deviating from the declared payroll and operational costs profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited annual financial statements, monthly management accounts reconciling the fleet dispatch revenue waterfall, the client subscription ledger export, source systems' route-optimization logs, purchase orders and driver payment settlement records, and an independent Swiss audit firm's Agreed-Upon-Procedures report on transaction completeness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to non-bank digital wallets, crypto-fiat bridges, or unregulated payment aggregators in the receivable structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cashflow architecture mapping proving all settlement mirrors pass through FINMA-regulated or equivalent EU/UK licensed banks; certified PCI-DSS and service-organization-control reports for the Stripe Billing integration, customer due-diligence files of the payment processor, and a written contractual prohibition on crypto conversion within the treasury operating agreement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be routed via a pure SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's bank using ISO 20022 purpose code CAPT (Capital Payment). The receiving Swiss bank requires a board resolution of the shareholder and the Swiss corporation recording the equity subscription, an updated shareholder register extract, a notarized statement of contribution, and the tax value declaration statement to the cantonal tax office. Funds may be held in a Capital Escrow Account segregated from operational treasuries until the commercial registry increase is completed. No SNB conversion approval is needed; the payment is credited in CHF or any freely convertible currency at the receiving bank's discretion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV messages cleared via Swiss SIX SIC/euroSIC rails, SEPA for EUR/CHF instantaneous where applicable, and the payment-versus-payment mechanism of CLS Bank for any simultaneous foreign exchange leg. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) are issued through the relationship corporate bank, with documentary presentation routed over SWIFT compatible 760/700 MT messages. For high-frequency operational billing, RICOCHET and Standing Settlement Instructions are applied to fleet dispatchers; payments are capped by transaction limits and matched against telematics verified trip invoices to avoid false-positive AML coordination.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery FX forwards on CHF/EUR/USD/GBP with a licensed Swiss bank counterparty under ISDA/DEF standard terms
FX swaps (swap-style forwards) used for short-term liquidity rollovers
Cross-currency swaps for long-term operational capital matching where interest exposure must be parallel hedged
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) restricted solely to non-fully-convertible currencies where a traditional deliverable forward is not available; not applicable to CHF, EUR, USD or GBP
Vanilla currency options (puts/calls) authorized for treasury risk only; no exotic barrier or leverage products

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return — Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal/Municipal Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and Cantonal Tax Administration of registered seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; extensions to 30 June or 31 December granted by cantonal practice upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a. on unpaid tax from the statutory due date; late-filing/precision penalties up to 100% of tax evaded; criminal proceedings for intentional or negligent tax evasion; assessment limitation period 5 years, extended to 10 years where facts were concealed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST) Settlement Return — quarterly, semi-annual or annual depending on declared turnover
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after expiry of each VAT reporting period; quarterly: 31 May / 31 Aug / 30 Nov / 28 Feb; annual settlement option only where turnover does not exceed CHF 5,005,000 under the Swiss VAT Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; administrative fine up to 25% of the VAT evaded; pro rata reduction of input VAT deduction; deletion of VAT registration for repeated failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Wage Declaration and Employer Contributions — AHV/IV/EO/ALV, SUVA, BVG and ancillary insurance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) of the registered office; SUVA for occupational accident insurance; BVG foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage statement and contribution settlement due by end of March of the following year; identical salary certificate to each employee by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late contribution interest on arrears; administrative penalty up to 100% of unpaid contributions; criminal prosecution for wilful omission; enforcement procedure against company assets by the compensation office

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Shareholders' Meeting, approval of financial statements and, where applicable, Commercial Register filing of board changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); publication via Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and Zefix
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting must be held within six months of the balance sheet date (calendar-year AG: by 30 June); any change to authorised signatories or capital must be filed within three months of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered dissolution if the company cannot validly convene its shareholders' meeting; administrative fines for late commercial register filings; additional notarial and publication costs; directors' personal liability for damages caused by missing filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Withholding Tax Declaration and Remittance (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends, profit shares and interest paid to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Federal Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment and declaration due by the 10th day of the month following the distribution; annual summary return within 30 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding tax liability at 35% becomes a strict company liability; default interest and penalty up to 100% of the unwithheld amount; criminal sanctions for intentional non-remittance; refund claims by shareholders permanently void if not reported

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 727: ordinary statutory audit is mandatory when the company exceeds two of the three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years — (a) balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, (b) turnover above CHF 40 million, (c) average more than 250 full-time employees. Companies below these thresholds may voluntarily opt for limited review (opting-up); companies with fewer than 10 full-time employees may obtain the shareholders' unanimous release from audit entirely (opting-out).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss statutory accounting under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 957–963; listed companies and larger groups shall apply IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER; tax authorities accept statutory financial statements as the assessment basis for federal, cantonal and municipal taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland introduced a mandatory beneficial-owners register for AGs on 1 July 2023. The register is not filed annually with a public authority; it must be updated by the AG within 30 days of any transfer of registered shares or any change in persons controlling the company (direct or indirect beneficial ownership of 25% or more). The register must be presented to the Federal Central Tax Office or the cantonal authorities upon request. No annual confirmation statement equivalent to the UK ARF or US annual report exists in Switzerland; record-keeping is an internal statutory duty. Intentional failure to record beneficial owners is a criminal offence punishable with fines up to CHF 100,000, and aggravated professional violations may be fined up to CHF 500,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders / Share Register (Aktienbuch) — showing registered shares, transfers and beneficial owners
Minutes of Board of Directors' meetings (Verwaltungsratsprotokolle)
Accounting books and records, including business correspondence and supporting vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 4,000 per annum (Zurich, Geneva and Zug; based on CHF 1,400 – 3,700 typical market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 for a typical small AG (turnover below CHF 2 million), assuming limited review unless opting-out is valid; up to USD 25,000 – 60,000 for full statutory audit of a mid-sized logistics-tech company requiring Swiss GAAP FER statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax imposed on after-tax profit (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal, cantonal and communal effective rate ranges from approximately 11.9% to 21.0% depending on the canton of residence of the AG.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory federal or cantonal tax holidays. Preferential measures applicable: (i) cantonal patent box exempting up to 90% of qualifying IP and royalty income; (ii) super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying research and development costs in participating cantons; (iii) notional interest deduction on qualifying excess equity in selected cantons; (iv) participation relief fully exempting dividends and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10% or with a holding value above CHF 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Joint cantonal and federal corporate income tax return for legal entities (German: Steuererklärung juristische Personen; French: formulaire pour personnes morales), filed through the competent Cantonal Tax Administration e-filing portal (e.g., eTax, ZugOnline, VaudTax) with consolidated data transmitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is generally six months after fiscal year-end; cantonal authorities routinely grant an extension of up to twelve months upon reasoned request. For calendar-year companies the initial deadline is typically set around 31 March of the following year. Failure to file after reminders triggers an estimated assessment by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), commercial register number (CHE), registered seat, fiscal year dates, NOGA/ISIC code and shareholder information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company without a Swiss permanent establishment leaves this section N/A and files no Swiss return; a limited return is lodged only where a Swiss PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory after-tax profit per the annual financial statements, adjusted for tax add-backs such as non-arm's-length expenses, hidden profit distributions and excessive director fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the profit attributable to the Swiss PE under the applicable DTA and Swiss cantonal allocation rules; foreign passive income is excluded absent Swiss nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of dividend income and capital gains on qualifying participations of at least 10% or with an acquisition value above CHF 1 million; supported by holding certificates and financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-resident shareholders are not eligible inside the Swiss return; Swiss withholding tax relief is obtained separately via refund under the DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Patent Box / IP Deduction (Lizenzboxabzug / Imposition réduite des revenus de brevets)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduction of qualifying royalty and IP income from patented software and embedded algorithms, including logistics-fleet dispatch IP; applicable at cantonal level with federal assessment limited to the federal proportion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to foreign-resident entities without a Swiss taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annex of prior-year assessed losses; losses offset taxable profit for up to seven consecutive years after the loss year; no loss carryback is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses economically connected to a Swiss PE may be carried forward in a non-resident limited return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 5,000 per federal or cantonal provision, reminder fees, and estimated assessment if no return is filed. Underreported tax: penalty of up to the evaded tax for simple evasion and up to three times the evaded tax in aggravated cases. Late payment: default interest of approximately 3.0% to 4.5% per annum on the assessed tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends paid by the Swiss AG from distributable profits; refundable to Swiss-resident beneficial owners and reduced or refundable under applicable double taxation agreements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the foreign parent must (i) obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (ii) file with the ESTV a refund application on Form 823 for legal entities or Form 824 for individuals, attaching the TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration and shareholding confirmation; (iii) submit the claim within three years from the end of the calendar year of the dividend payment. Relief at source is allowed only under the approved advance-filing procedure; otherwise 35% is withheld and refunded upon approval. Under the Switzerland–PRC DTA the reduced dividend rate is 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the paying company's capital and 10% in all other cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties and intercompany arm's-length interest is 0%; only interest on Swiss public bonds and bank deposits is subject to the 35% Verrechnungssteuer. Under the Switzerland–PRC DTA, the treaty rate is 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and the principal purpose test.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland follows the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. Mandatory Local File documentation is required where related-party transactions exceed CHF 5 million in a tax period or the Swiss entity reports annual gross revenue of CHF 80 million or more; a Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900 million; Country-by-Country reporting applies above the same CHF 900 million group revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a statutory Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or BVI; however, Swiss GAAR, the MLI Principal Purpose Test effective since 1 January 2022, and DTA beneficial ownership rules impose an equivalent factual substance requirement. The Swiss AG must maintain genuine premises, qualified personnel, active board decisions and substantive management in Switzerland; a letterbox holding company for logistics-tech IP or fleet-dispatch SaaS royalties is exposed to recharacterization of income, denial of treaty relief, revocation of cantonal tax rulings and criminal tax exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing an incomplete or false corporate income tax return, fabricating deductible expenses, concealing taxable Swiss-source profit from the logistics-fleet dispatch SaaS, or using forged documents to support false deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Simple evasion: administrative penalty of up to the amount of the evaded tax (up to three times the evaded tax in aggravated cases) plus recovery of tax and interest; qualified tax fraud: fine of up to CHF 30,000 per offense and full restitution of tax and penalties; prosecution under the Federal Criminal Administrative Law (VStrR) may result in custodial sentences of up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false returns bear individual criminal liability; the corporate veil may be pierced for civil restitution; serious cases trigger seizure of personal assets, travel bans in mutual legal assistance procedures, and extradition exposure under international arrest notices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to foreign shareholders without deducting and remitting the 35% Swiss withholding tax, or disguising distributions as current-account payments, inflated management fees or excessive software license payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AG is liable for the unremitted 35% withholding tax plus late-payment interest; additional penal surcharges are imposed for negligent non-collection; proceedings under the Swiss Withholding Tax Act can yield fines equivalent to the tax withheld and punitive interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable under Article 13 of the Withholding Tax Act for the duties of collection and remittance; criminal sentences of up to three years and personal asset seizure are available in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing in intercompany SaaS licensing, fleet telematics services, management fees, or interest paid to related offshore entities; circular transactions with no commercial rationale and artificial profit stripping from Swiss revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment reallocating profit to Switzerland; secondary adjustment treating the excess as a constructive dividend subject to 35% withholding tax; penalty interest; fines of up to three times the evaded tax; denial of deductions; denial of treaty benefits under the MLI principal purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be sued under Article 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations for corporate damage caused by tax restitution and penalties; criminal exposure for aiding tax evasion may lead to imprisonment, travel bans and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a letterbox entity holding logistics-tech IP or SaaS royalties without employees, premises or real board decision-making, for the sole purpose of accessing Swiss treaty benefits or preferential cantonal taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; recharacterization of license fees as constructive dividends; retroactive reassessment with default interest; revocation of cantonal tax privileges; administrative fines up to CHF 30,000 per offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for restitution of unpaid taxes and lost treaty benefits; criminal exposure for intentional abuse; in cross-border structures directors may face international asset freezes and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial Ownership and Transparency Register Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain the shareholder register, bearer-share records or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) documentation of the CH_AG in the commercial register and before banking and payment-rail counterparties such as Stripe Billing and wire-transfer banks, despite the low-risk AML tier.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Swiss Code of Obligations of up to CHF 10,000 per violation; forced deregistration of the entity; banking partners may freeze payment rails and terminate merchant agreements; persistent non-compliance blocks issuance of Swiss tax clearance certificates and notarial certificates of good standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors and officers are personally liable for the fines and for resulting damages to creditors and authorities; serious breaches can lead to disqualification from board office, criminal registration and, in cross-border cases, travel restrictions.
